newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Lufthansa "pioneers" Hong Kong bar coding.
newsitem.headline: Lufthansa "pioneers" Hong Kong bar coding.

text.p: Lufthansa Cargo will become the first airline to barcode all air freight when it pioneers a pilot scheme in Hong Kong on July 1st, according to a member of the airline's executive board, Stefan Lauer.

Briefing reporters on the "innovation," Lauer said he hopes barcoding will be introduced throughout the airline's world wide system next spring. He said Lufthansa Cargo was leading the way and expects barcoding to eventually become industry standard.

Twenty of the airline's contract freight forwarding companies in Hong Kong have invested HK$15,000 ($1,930) each in barcoding technology and printing systems to enable the scheme to start. Lufthansa said the investment will quickly be paid off in benefits such as reduced workload for forwarders and less errors.
Another new product to be tested in Hong Kong will be improvements to the carrier's FLASH express service, Lauer added but gave no details.

Hong Kong is also leading the way in a new "tripartite approach" involving airline managers, freight forwarders and customers to find ways to improve service and find tailor-made solutions to customer needs.

"We have had the first very encouraging success in Hong Kong. We are quite confident that this new approach is the right one. We have to act more together. I am convinced that the time of the lonely hunter in our business if effectively over," Lauer said.
